questions.question: An analyst declares marks and encodings in Python and the library compiles the chart to a Vega-Lite JSON spec rendered in the browser. Which declarative library is she using?
questions.explanation: Altair is a declarative Python visualization library whose charts are Vega-Lite specifications, following the Grammar of Graphics.

questions.question: A newsroom builds a fully custom interactive graphic by binding data to SVG DOM elements with low-level control over every transition. Which JavaScript library does this?
questions.explanation: D3.js (Data-Driven Documents) binds data to DOM elements, giving low-level control for bespoke interactive visualizations.

questions.question: A strip plot of hundreds of points stacked on discrete category ticks hides most of the data; the analyst nudges each point by a small random offset. What technique fixes the overplotting?
questions.explanation: Jittering adds small random noise to point positions so overlapping marks become individually visible.

questions.question: To compare cars on mpg, horsepower, weight, and price simultaneously, each car is drawn as a single polyline crossing a set of vertical axes, one per variable. Which plot is this?
questions.explanation: A parallel coordinates plot draws each observation as a polyline across parallel axes, one axis per variable, enabling multivariate comparison.

questions.question: A team embeds 10,000 images in 50-dimensional space and needs a 2-D map that keeps neighboring points together by modeling pairwise similarities with a Student-t distribution in the low-dimensional space. Which technique produces this plot?
questions.explanation: t-SNE converts high-dimensional similarities into probabilities and matches them with a heavy-tailed Student-t distribution in 2-D, preserving local neighborhoods.

questions.question: A dashboard shows how website visitors split and merge through landing page, signup, and purchase, with band widths proportional to the number flowing between stages. Which diagram is this?
questions.explanation: A Sankey diagram draws flows between nodes with widths proportional to quantity, unlike a funnel which only shows a single shrinking sequence.

questions.question: A report shades each US state from light to dark according to its voter-turnout rate. Which map type is this?
questions.explanation: A choropleth encodes a data value as the fill color of each geographic region, unlike proportional symbol maps which size markers instead.

questions.question: A data scientist wants an interactive slippy map inside a Python notebook, rendered with Leaflet.js tiles. Which library should she use?
questions.explanation: Folium generates interactive Leaflet.js maps directly from Python objects such as DataFrames.

questions.question: A dense scatter plot hides point density, so the analyst sets alpha = 0.1 so that overlapping points darken into visible density regions. What technique is this?
questions.explanation: Alpha blending renders marks semi-transparent so overlapping points accumulate ink and reveal density.

questions.question: A forecast figure shows the predicted mean as a line plus a shaded band for the 95% interval that widens over time. Which chart type is this?
questions.explanation: A ribbon (area-range) chart fills the band between a lower and upper bound over time, displaying uncertainty alongside the central line.

questions.question: Which chart should you use to show customer drop-off between sequential stages of a sales process?
questions.explanation: Funnel charts show shrinking values through sequential process stages.

questions.question: On an election map, states are resized so that each state's area encodes its electoral-vote count rather than its land area. What kind of map is this?
questions.explanation: A cartogram distorts region geometry so that area represents a statistic such as population or electoral votes.

questions.question: A gene-expression heatmap must reorder its rows and columns by hierarchical clustering and draw dendrograms along both margins. Which seaborn function produces this?
questions.explanation: seaborn.clustermap hierarchically clusters rows and columns of a heatmap and draws the dendrograms alongside it.

questions.question: To check normality of residuals, an analyst plots the sorted sample quantiles against the theoretical quantiles of a normal distribution and looks for a straight line. Which plot is this?
questions.explanation: A Q-Q plot compares sample and theoretical quantiles; points hugging the reference line indicate agreement with the reference distribution.

questions.question: An analyst needs one scatter plot per penguin species arranged in a grid sharing axes, by mapping one plotting function over data subsets. Which seaborn object does this?
questions.explanation: FacetGrid maps a plotting function across a grid of conditional subsets defined by categorical variables.

questions.question: A quality dashboard must show defect causes as bars sorted in descending order plus a cumulative percentage line to highlight the 'vital few'. Which chart is this?
questions.explanation: A Pareto chart combines descending bars with a cumulative line, embodying the 80/20 principle.

questions.question: An analyst wants to show how the ranking of 8 products changed between last year and this year, with one line per product connecting its two ranks. Which chart fits best?
questions.explanation: A slope chart (or bump chart for rankings) connects each item's value or rank across two points, emphasizing changes in position.

questions.question: A scatter plot of 500,000 points is an unreadable blob of overlapping marks. Instead of adding jitter, which technique aggregates points into hexagonal cells colored by count?
questions.explanation: Hexbin plots bin the plane into hexagons and encode density by color, solving massive overplotting.

questions.question: A storage dashboard shows disk usage as nested rectangles: each top-level folder is a rectangle sized by its bytes, with subfolders nested inside it. Which chart is this?
questions.explanation: A treemap displays hierarchical part-to-whole data as nested rectangles whose areas are proportional to the values.

questions.question: A report needs a map where a sized bubble centered on each country encodes its GDP per capita. Which visualization is this?
questions.explanation: Proportional symbol maps scale point symbols over regions by a data value, unlike choropleths which shade region fill color.
